# Ondo Finance Founder Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 32

The decentralized finance community is mourning the sudden passing of Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of real-world asset (RWA) platform Ondo Finance. The company confirmed on [May 26, 2026](https://x.com/OndoFinance/status/2059054473775894797?ref=blockhead.co), that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

## FAQs

He was a widely respected pioneer for his work in bringing traditional financial assets like U.S. Treasuries onto the blockchain, drawing on his experience from Goldman Sachs and the crypto industry.

**2. Who is the new CEO of Ondo Finance?**

The new CEO of Ondo Finance is Ian De Bode. He previously served as the company's president and chief strategy officer. His appointment was part of a planned succession, ensuring leadership continuity.

**3. How did the ONDO token react to the news?**

The ONDO governance token saw a mild decline of about 3%, trading near $0.43 in the 24 hours after the news. This relative stability is seen by many as a sign of the market's confidence in the company's resilience and its new leadership.

data.systemPrompt:
You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.
## Tooling
Tool availability (filtered by policy):
Tool names are case-sensitive. Call tools exactly as listed.
- read: Read file contents
- write: Create or overwrite files
- edit: Make precise edits to files
- exec: Run shell commands (pty available for TTY-required CLIs)
- process: Manage background exec sessions
- web_search: Search the web (Brave API)
- web_fetch: Fetch and extract readable content from a URL
- browser: Control web browser
- canvas: Present/eval/snapshot the Canvas
- message: Send messages and channel actions
- agents_list: List OpenClaw agent ids allowed for sessions_spawn when runtime="subagent" (not ACP harness ids)
- sessions_list: List other sessions (incl. sub-agents) with filters/last
- sessions_history: Fetch history for another session/sub-agent
- sessions_send: Send a message to another session/sub-agent
- subagents: List, steer, or kill sub-agent runs for this requester session
- session_status: Show a /status-equivalent status card (usage + time + Reasoning/Verbose/Elevated); use for model-use questions (📊 session_status); optional per-session model override
- image_generate: Generate images with the configured image-generation model
- memory_get
- memory_search
- sessions_spawn: Spawn a sub-agent or ACP coding session; defaults to isolated, native subagents may use context="fork" when current transcript context is required (runtime="acp" requires `agentId` unless `acp.defaultAgent` is configured; ACP harness ids follow acp.allowedAgents, not agents_list)
- sessions_yield
- tts
TOOLS.md does not control tool availability; it is user guidance for how to use external tools.
For long waits, avoid rapid poll loops: use exec with enough yieldMs or process(action=poll, timeout=<ms>).

# EDITORIAL_FEEDBACK.md — News Card Editorial Feedback

Handles Telegram feedback on published news cards. **Not part of the crypto pipeline.**

---

## When this applies

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Callback `oc_r:` / `oc_ri:` / `oc_ri_menu:` | Rate article or image |
| Callback `oc_draft:` / `oc_draft_yes:` / `oc_draft_no:` | Unpublish flow |
| Callback `oc_publish:` / `oc_publish_yes:` / `oc_publish_no:` | Publish flow |
| Callback `oc_edit:` / `oc_edit_apply:` / `oc_edit_cancel:` | Edit flow |
| Text | `RATE 8`, `IMAGE 7`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` |
| Document reply | `.md` file replying to bot's edit prompt |

---

## What to do

1. **Do NOT** start or continue the crypto news pipeline.
2. **Do NOT** spawn subagents.
3. Run the handler immediately:

```bash
python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace-orchestrator/skills/pipeline/handle_card_feedback.py \
  --payload "<callback data if present>" \
  --message-text "<user text if present>" \
  --chat-id "<telegram chat id>" \
  --user-id "<telegram user id>" \
  --username "<telegram username if known>" \
  --reply-to-message-id "<replied-to message id if present>" \
  --document-file-id "<telegram file_id if document upload>" \
  --document-name "<original filename if document upload>"
```

4. **If the handler already sent a Telegram reply, do NOT repeat stdout in the group — end turn silently.**
5. If handler failed before replying, show the stdout line to the user.

---

## Pipeline vs feedback

| User says | Route |
|-----------|-------|
| `run pipeline`, `run crypto news pipeline` | SOUL.md pipeline |
| RATE, IMAGE, DRAFT, PUBLISH, EDIT, callback taps, edit `.md` upload | This doc |

Pipeline takes precedence only when the message explicitly requests the pipeline.

---

## PUBLISH flow notes

- Tap **Publish** or reply `PUBLISH` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, publish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `publish` (live on site).
- If already published → bot replies "already published".

---

## EDIT flow notes

- Tap **Edit** or reply `EDIT` to the news card.
- Bot sends `article-{run_id}.md` as a document.
- Download → edit → **save** → reply to that document with a corrected **`.md` file** (not pasted text).
- Identical upload (no changes) → bot replies "No changes detected" and keeps the edit session open (`EDIT_UNCHANGED`).
- Changed upload → bot shows **+N / −M lines** summary plus **Apply to WordPress** / **Cancel** buttons.
- After apply on a draft → bot offers a **Publish** button on the confirmation message.
- Pasted text during edit → handler returns `EDIT_USE_DOCUMENT`.

### Document reply — CRITICAL routing rule

When the user replies to the bot's edit prompt with a `.md` document:

1. **Always** call the handler with `--document-file-id` from the **user's uploaded document** in the current message metadata.
2. **Never** read `media/inbound/tmp*.md` from reply context — that is often the **bot's original unedited file** bundled with the user's upload.
3. **Never** call `handle_edit_document()` manually with a local path. The handler downloads the file from Telegram via `file_id`.
4. Set `--reply-to-message-id` to the **bot edit prompt message id** (the document the user replied to).

Wrong file selection causes false `EDIT_UNCHANGED` even when the user's saved file has real edits.

---

## DRAFT flow notes

- Tap **Unpublish** or reply `DRAFT` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, unpublish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `draft`.

---

## Mention rules

- Callback taps: no `@mention` needed.
- Reply to news card: `RATE`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` work without `@mention`.
- Reply to bot edit prompt with `.md`: works via `reply_to_bot` implicit mention.

# Ondo Finance Founder Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 32

The decentralized finance community is mourning the sudden passing of Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of real-world asset (RWA) platform Ondo Finance. The company confirmed on [May 26, 2026](https://x.com/OndoFinance/status/2059054473775894797?ref=blockhead.co), that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

# Ondo Finance Founder Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 32

The decentralized finance community is mourning the sudden passing of Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of real-world asset (RWA) platform Ondo Finance. The company confirmed on May 26, 2026, that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

Nathan Allman was the founder and CEO of Ondo Finance, a leading platform for real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. He was a widely respected pioneer for his work in bringing traditional financial assets like U.S. Treasuries onto the blockchain, drawing on his experience from Goldman Sachs and the crypto industry.

**2. Who is the new CEO of Ondo Finance?**

The new CEO of Ondo Finance is Ian De Bode. He previously served as the company's president and chief strategy officer. His appointment was part of a planned succession, ensuring leadership continuity.

**3. How did the ONDO token react to the news?**

The ONDO governance token saw a mild decline of about 3%, trading near $0.43 in the 24 hours after the news. This relative stability is seen by many as a sign of the market's confidence in the company's resilience and its new leadership.

content.text:
# EDITORIAL_FEEDBACK.md — News Card Editorial Feedback

Handles Telegram feedback on published news cards. **Not part of the crypto pipeline.**

---

## When this applies

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Callback `oc_r:` / `oc_ri:` / `oc_ri_menu:` | Rate article or image |
| Callback `oc_draft:` / `oc_draft_yes:` / `oc_draft_no:` | Unpublish flow |
| Callback `oc_publish:` / `oc_publish_yes:` / `oc_publish_no:` | Publish flow |
| Callback `oc_edit:` / `oc_edit_apply:` / `oc_edit_cancel:` | Edit flow |
| Text | `RATE 8`, `IMAGE 7`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` |
| Document reply | `.md` file replying to bot's edit prompt |

---

## What to do

1. **Do NOT** start or continue the crypto news pipeline.
2. **Do NOT** spawn subagents.
3. Run the handler immediately:

```bash
python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace-orchestrator/skills/pipeline/handle_card_feedback.py \
  --payload "<callback data if present>" \
  --message-text "<user text if present>" \
  --chat-id "<telegram chat id>" \
  --user-id "<telegram user id>" \
  --username "<telegram username if known>" \
  --reply-to-message-id "<replied-to message id if present>" \
  --document-file-id "<telegram file_id if document upload>" \
  --document-name "<original filename if document upload>"
```

4. **If the handler already sent a Telegram reply, do NOT repeat stdout in the group — end turn silently.**
5. If handler failed before replying, show the stdout line to the user.

---

## Pipeline vs feedback

| User says | Route |
|-----------|-------|
| `run pipeline`, `run crypto news pipeline` | SOUL.md pipeline |
| RATE, IMAGE, DRAFT, PUBLISH, EDIT, callback taps, edit `.md` upload | This doc |

Pipeline takes precedence only when the message explicitly requests the pipeline.

---

## PUBLISH flow notes

- Tap **Publish** or reply `PUBLISH` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, publish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `publish` (live on site).
- If already published → bot replies "already published".

---

## EDIT flow notes

- Tap **Edit** or reply `EDIT` to the news card.
- Bot sends `article-{run_id}.md` as a document.
- Download → edit → **save** → reply to that document with a corrected **`.md` file** (not pasted text).
- Identical upload (no changes) → bot replies "No changes detected" and keeps the edit session open (`EDIT_UNCHANGED`).
- Changed upload → bot shows **+N / −M lines** summary plus **Apply to WordPress** / **Cancel** buttons.
- After apply on a draft → bot offers a **Publish** button on the confirmation message.
- Pasted text during edit → handler returns `EDIT_USE_DOCUMENT`.

### Document reply — CRITICAL routing rule

When the user replies to the bot's edit prompt with a `.md` document:

1. **Always** call the handler with `--document-file-id` from the **user's uploaded document** in the current message metadata.
2. **Never** read `media/inbound/tmp*.md` from reply context — that is often the **bot's original unedited file** bundled with the user's upload.
3. **Never** call `handle_edit_document()` manually with a local path. The handler downloads the file from Telegram via `file_id`.
4. Set `--reply-to-message-id` to the **bot edit prompt message id** (the document the user replied to).

Wrong file selection causes false `EDIT_UNCHANGED` even when the user's saved file has real edits.

---

## DRAFT flow notes

- Tap **Unpublish** or reply `DRAFT` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, unpublish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `draft`.

---

## Mention rules

- Callback taps: no `@mention` needed.
- Reply to news card: `RATE`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` work without `@mention`.
- Reply to bot edit prompt with `.md`: works via `reply_to_bot` implicit mention.

# Ondo Finance Founder Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 32

The decentralized finance community is mourning the sudden passing of Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of real-world asset (RWA) platform Ondo Finance. The company confirmed on [May 26, 2026](https://x.com/OndoFinance/status/2059054473775894797?ref=blockhead.co), that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

## FAQs

Nathan Allman was the founder and CEO of Ondo Finance, a leading platform for real-world asset (RWA) tokenization. He was a widely respected pioneer for his work in bringing traditional financial assets like U.S. Treasuries onto the blockchain, drawing on his experience from Goldman Sachs and the crypto industry.

**2. Who is the new CEO of Ondo Finance?**

The new CEO of Ondo Finance is Ian De Bode. He previously served as the company's president and chief strategy officer. His appointment was part of a planned succession, ensuring leadership continuity.

**3. How did the ONDO token react to the news?**

The ONDO governance token saw a mild decline of about 3%, trading near $0.43 in the 24 hours after the news. This relative stability is seen by many as a sign of the market's confidence in the company's resilience and its new leadership.

# EDITORIAL_FEEDBACK.md — News Card Editorial Feedback

Handles Telegram feedback on published news cards. **Not part of the crypto pipeline.**

---

## When this applies

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Callback `oc_r:` / `oc_ri:` / `oc_ri_menu:` | Rate article or image |
| Callback `oc_draft:` / `oc_draft_yes:` / `oc_draft_no:` | Unpublish flow |
| Callback `oc_publish:` / `oc_publish_yes:` / `oc_publish_no:` | Publish flow |
| Callback `oc_edit:` / `oc_edit_apply:` / `oc_edit_cancel:` | Edit flow |
| Text | `RATE 8`, `IMAGE 7`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` |
| Document reply | `.md` file replying to bot's edit prompt |

---

## What to do

1. **Do NOT** start or continue the crypto news pipeline.
2. **Do NOT** spawn subagents.
3. Run the handler immediately:

```bash
python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace-orchestrator/skills/pipeline/handle_card_feedback.py \
  --payload "<callback data if present>" \
  --message-text "<user text if present>" \
  --chat-id "<telegram chat id>" \
  --user-id "<telegram user id>" \
  --username "<telegram username if known>" \
  --reply-to-message-id "<replied-to message id if present>" \
  --document-file-id "<telegram file_id if document upload>" \
  --document-name "<original filename if document upload>"
```

4. **If the handler already sent a Telegram reply, do NOT repeat stdout in the group — end turn silently.**
5. If handler failed before replying, show the stdout line to the user.

---

## Pipeline vs feedback

| User says | Route |
|-----------|-------|
| `run pipeline`, `run crypto news pipeline` | SOUL.md pipeline |
| RATE, IMAGE, DRAFT, PUBLISH, EDIT, callback taps, edit `.md` upload | This doc |

Pipeline takes precedence only when the message explicitly requests the pipeline.

---

## PUBLISH flow notes

- Tap **Publish** or reply `PUBLISH` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, publish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `publish` (live on site).
- If already published → bot replies "already published".

---

## EDIT flow notes

- Tap **Edit** or reply `EDIT` to the news card.
- Bot sends `article-{run_id}.md` as a document.
- Download → edit → **save** → reply to that document with a corrected **`.md` file** (not pasted text).
- Identical upload (no changes) → bot replies "No changes detected" and keeps the edit session open (`EDIT_UNCHANGED`).
- Changed upload → bot shows **+N / −M lines** summary plus **Apply to WordPress** / **Cancel** buttons.
- After apply on a draft → bot offers a **Publish** button on the confirmation message.
- Pasted text during edit → handler returns `EDIT_USE_DOCUMENT`.

### Document reply — CRITICAL routing rule

When the user replies to the bot's edit prompt with a `.md` document:

1. **Always** call the handler with `--document-file-id` from the **user's uploaded document** in the current message metadata.
2. **Never** read `media/inbound/tmp*.md` from reply context — that is often the **bot's original unedited file** bundled with the user's upload.
3. **Never** call `handle_edit_document()` manually with a local path. The handler downloads the file from Telegram via `file_id`.
4. Set `--reply-to-message-id` to the **bot edit prompt message id** (the document the user replied to).

Wrong file selection causes false `EDIT_UNCHANGED` even when the user's saved file has real edits.

---

## DRAFT flow notes

- Tap **Unpublish** or reply `DRAFT` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, unpublish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `draft`.

---

## Mention rules

- Callback taps: no `@mention` needed.
- Reply to news card: `RATE`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` work without `@mention`.
- Reply to bot edit prompt with `.md`: works via `reply_to_bot` implicit mention.

# Ondo Finance Founder Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 32

The decentralized finance community is mourning the sudden passing of Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of real-world asset (RWA) platform Ondo Finance. The company confirmed on [May 26, 2026](https://x.com/OndoFinance/status/2059054473775894797?ref=blockhead.co), that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

## FAQs

He was a widely respected pioneer for his work in bringing traditional financial assets like U.S. Treasuries onto the blockchain, drawing on his experience from Goldman Sachs and the crypto industry.

**2. Who is the new CEO of Ondo Finance?**

The new CEO of Ondo Finance is Ian De Bode. He previously served as the company's president and chief strategy officer. His appointment was part of a planned succession, ensuring leadership continuity.

**3. How did the ONDO token react to the news?**

The ONDO governance token saw a mild decline of about 3%, trading near $0.43 in the 24 hours after the news. This relative stability is seen by many as a sign of the market's confidence in the company's resilience and its new leadership.

# EDITORIAL_FEEDBACK.md — News Card Editorial Feedback

Handles Telegram feedback on published news cards. **Not part of the crypto pipeline.**

---

## When this applies

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Callback `oc_r:` / `oc_ri:` / `oc_ri_menu:` | Rate article or image |
| Callback `oc_draft:` / `oc_draft_yes:` / `oc_draft_no:` | Unpublish flow |
| Callback `oc_publish:` / `oc_publish_yes:` / `oc_publish_no:` | Publish flow |
| Callback `oc_edit:` / `oc_edit_apply:` / `oc_edit_cancel:` | Edit flow |
| Text | `RATE 8`, `IMAGE 7`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` |
| Document reply | `.md` file replying to bot's edit prompt |

---

## What to do

1. **Do NOT** start or continue the crypto news pipeline.
2. **Do NOT** spawn subagents.
3. Run the handler immediately:

```bash
python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace-orchestrator/skills/pipeline/handle_card_feedback.py \
  --payload "<callback data if present>" \
  --message-text "<user text if present>" \
  --chat-id "<telegram chat id>" \
  --user-id "<telegram user id>" \
  --username "<telegram username if known>" \
  --reply-to-message-id "<replied-to message id if present>" \
  --document-file-id "<telegram file_id if document upload>" \
  --document-name "<original filename if document upload>"
```

4. **If the handler already sent a Telegram reply, do NOT repeat stdout in the group — end turn silently.**
5. If handler failed before replying, show the stdout line to the user.

---

## Pipeline vs feedback

| User says | Route |
|-----------|-------|
| `run pipeline`, `run crypto news pipeline` | SOUL.md pipeline |
| RATE, IMAGE, DRAFT, PUBLISH, EDIT, callback taps, edit `.md` upload | This doc |

Pipeline takes precedence only when the message explicitly requests the pipeline.

---

## PUBLISH flow notes

- Tap **Publish** or reply `PUBLISH` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, publish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `publish` (live on site).
- If already published → bot replies "already published".

---

## EDIT flow notes

- Tap **Edit** or reply `EDIT` to the news card.
- Bot sends `article-{run_id}.md` as a document.
- Download → edit → **save** → reply to that document with a corrected **`.md` file** (not pasted text).
- Identical upload (no changes) → bot replies "No changes detected" and keeps the edit session open (`EDIT_UNCHANGED`).
- Changed upload → bot shows **+N / −M lines** summary plus **Apply to WordPress** / **Cancel** buttons.
- After apply on a draft → bot offers a **Publish** button on the confirmation message.
- Pasted text during edit → handler returns `EDIT_USE_DOCUMENT`.

### Document reply — CRITICAL routing rule

When the user replies to the bot's edit prompt with a `.md` document:

1. **Always** call the handler with `--document-file-id` from the **user's uploaded document** in the current message metadata.
2. **Never** read `media/inbound/tmp*.md` from reply context — that is often the **bot's original unedited file** bundled with the user's upload.
3. **Never** call `handle_edit_document()` manually with a local path. The handler downloads the file from Telegram via `file_id`.
4. Set `--reply-to-message-id` to the **bot edit prompt message id** (the document the user replied to).

Wrong file selection causes false `EDIT_UNCHANGED` even when the user's saved file has real edits.

---

## DRAFT flow notes

- Tap **Unpublish** or reply `DRAFT` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, unpublish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `draft`.

---

## Mention rules

- Callback taps: no `@mention` needed.
- Reply to news card: `RATE`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` work without `@mention`.
- Reply to bot edit prompt with `.md`: works via `reply_to_bot` implicit mention.

The company confirmed on [May 26, 2026](https://x.com/OndoFinance/status/2059054473775894797?ref=blockhead.co), that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

tools.name: agents_list
tools.description: List OpenClaw agent ids you can target with `sessions_spawn` when `runtime="subagent"` (based on subagent allowlists).

tools.name: browser
tools.description: Control the browser via OpenClaw's browser control server (status/start/stop/profiles/tabs/open/snapshot/screenshot/actions). Browser choice: omit profile by default for the isolated OpenClaw-managed browser (`openclaw`). For the logged-in user browser, use profile="user". A supported Chromium-based browser (v144+) must be running on the selected host or browser node. Use only when existing logins/cookies matter and the user is present. When a node-hosted browser proxy is available, the tool may auto-route to it. Pin a node with node=<id|name> or target="node". When using refs from snapshot (e.g. e12), keep the same tab: prefer passing targetId from the snapshot response into subsequent actions (act/click/type/etc). For stable, self-resolving refs across calls, use snapshot with refs="aria" (Playwright aria-ref ids). Default refs="role" are role+name-based. Use snapshot+act for UI automation. Avoid act:wait by default; use only in exceptional cases when no reliable UI state exists. target selects browser location (sandbox|host|node). Default: host. Host target allowed.

tools.name: canvas
tools.description: Control node canvases (present/hide/navigate/eval/snapshot/A2UI). Use snapshot to capture the rendered UI.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: exec
tools.description: Execute shell commands with background continuation for work that starts now. Use yieldMs/background to continue later via process tool. For long-running work started now, rely on automatic completion wake when it is enabled and the command emits output or fails; otherwise use process to confirm completion. Use process whenever you need logs, status, input, or intervention. Use pty=true for TTY-required commands (terminal UIs, coding agents).

background.description: Run in background immediately

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, kills process on expiry)

pty.description: Run in a pseudo-terminal (PTY) when available (TTY-required CLIs, coding agents)

elevated.description: Run on the host with elevated permissions (if allowed)

tools.name: image_generate
tools.description: Generate new images or edit reference images with the configured or inferred image-generation model. Set agents.defaults.imageGenerationModel.primary to pick a provider/model. Providers declare their own auth/readiness; use action="list" to inspect registered providers, models, readiness, and auth hints. Generated images are delivered automatically from the tool result as MEDIA paths.

action.description: Optional action: "generate" (default) or "list" to inspect available providers/models.

image.description: Optional reference image path or URL for edit mode.

images.description: Optional reference images for edit mode (up to 5).

filename.description: Optional output filename hint. OpenClaw preserves the basename and saves under its managed media directory.

resolution.description: Optional resolution hint: 1K, 2K, or 4K. Useful for Google edit/generation flows.

quality.description: Optional quality hint: low, medium, high, or auto when the provider supports it.

outputFormat.description: Optional output format hint: png, jpeg, or webp when the provider supports it.

background.description: OpenAI-only background hint: transparent, opaque, or auto.

moderation.description: OpenAI-only moderation hint: low or auto.

outputCompression.description: OpenAI-only compression level for jpeg/webp outputFormat, 0-100.

user.description: OpenAI-only stable end-user identifier for abuse monitoring.

count.description: Optional number of images to request (1-4).

timeoutMs.description: Optional provider request timeout in milliseconds.

tools.name: memory_get
tools.description: Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.

tools.name: memory_search
tools.description: Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. Optional `corpus=wiki` or `corpus=all` also searches registered compiled-wiki supplements. If response has disabled=true, memory retrieval is unavailable and should be surfaced to the user.

tools.name: message
tools.description: Send, delete, and manage messages via channel plugins. Current channel (telegram) supports: delete, edit, poll, react, send, topic-create, topic-edit.

items.description: Recipient/channel targets (same format as --target); accepts ids or names when the directory is available.

effectId.description: Message effect name/id for sendWithEffect (e.g., invisible ink).

media.description: Media URL or local path. data: URLs are not supported here, use buffer.

buffer.description: Base64 payload for attachments (optionally a data: URL).

forceDocument.description: Send image/GIF as document to avoid Telegram compression (Telegram only).

asDocument.description: Send image/GIF as document to avoid Telegram compression. Alias for forceDocument (Telegram only).

presentation.description: Shared presentation payload for rich text, buttons, selects, and context. Core degrades unsupported blocks to text.

delivery.description: Shared delivery preferences. pin requests that the sent message be pinned when the channel supports it.

messageId.description: Target message id for reaction. If omitted, defaults to the current inbound message id when available.

message_id.description: snake_case alias of messageId. If omitted, defaults to the current inbound message id when available.

pollOptionId.description: Poll answer id to vote for. Use when the channel exposes stable answer ids.

items.description: Poll answer ids to vote for in a multiselect poll. Use when the channel exposes stable answer ids.

pollOptionIndex.description: 1-based poll option number to vote for, matching the rendered numbered poll choices.

items.description: 1-based poll option numbers to vote for in a multiselect poll, matching the rendered numbered poll choices.

chatId.description: Chat id for chat-scoped metadata actions.

items.description: Channel id filter (repeatable).

image.description: Cover image URL or local file path for the event.

clearParent.description: Clear the parent/category when supported by the provider.

activityType.description: Activity type: playing, streaming, listening, watching, competing, custom.

activityUrl.description: Streaming URL (Twitch or YouTube). Only used with streaming type; may not render for bots.

activityState.description: State text. For custom type this is the status text; for others it shows in the flyout.

status.description: Bot status: online, dnd, idle, invisible.

tools.name: process
tools.description: Manage running exec sessions for commands already started: list, poll, log, write, send-keys, submit, paste, kill. Use poll/log when you need status, logs, quiet-success confirmation, or completion confirmation when automatic completion wake is unavailable. Use write/send-keys/submit/paste/kill for input or intervention.

action.description: Process action

keys.description: Key tokens to send for send-keys

hex.description: Hex bytes to send for send-keys

limit.description: Log length

timeout.description: For poll: wait up to this many milliseconds before returning

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: session_status
tools.description: Show a /status-equivalent session status card for the current or another visible session, including usage, time, cost when available, and linked background task context. Optional `model` sets a per-session model override; `model=default` resets overrides. Use this for questions like what model is active or how a session is configured.

tools.name: sessions_history
tools.description: Fetch sanitized message history for a visible session. Supports limits and optional tool messages; use this to inspect another session before replying, debugging, or resuming work.

tools.name: sessions_list
tools.description: List visible sessions with optional filters for kind, label, agentId, search, recent activity, derived titles, and last-message previews. Use this to discover a target session before calling sessions_history or sessions_send.

tools.name: sessions_send
tools.description: Send a message into another visible session by sessionKey or label. Use this to delegate follow-up work to an existing session; waits for the target run and returns the updated assistant reply when available.

tools.name: sessions_spawn
tools.description: Spawn a clean isolated session by default with `runtime="subagent"` or `runtime="acp"`. `mode="run"` is one-shot and `mode="session"` is persistent or thread-bound. Subagents inherit the parent workspace directory automatically. For native subagents only, set `context="fork"` when the child needs the current transcript context; otherwise omit it or use `context="isolated"`. Use this when the work should happen in a fresh child session instead of the current one.

resumeSessionId.description: Resume an existing agent session by its ID (e.g. a Codex session UUID from ~/.codex/sessions/). Requires runtime="acp". The agent replays conversation history via session/load instead of starting fresh.

context.description: Native subagent context mode. Omit or use "isolated" for a clean child session; use "fork" only when the child needs the requester transcript context.

lightContext.description: When true, spawned subagent runs use lightweight bootstrap context. Only applies to runtime='subagent'.

tools.name: sessions_yield
tools.description: End your current turn. Use after spawning subagents to receive their results as the next message.

tools.name: subagents
tools.description: List, kill, or steer spawned sub-agents for this requester session. Use this for sub-agent orchestration.

tools.name: tts

channel.description: Optional channel id to pick output format.

timeoutMs.description: Optional provider request timeout in milliseconds.

tools.name: web_fetch
tools.description: Fetch and extract readable content from a URL (HTML → markdown/text). Use for lightweight page access without browser automation.

url.description: HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch.

maxChars.description: Maximum characters to return (truncates when exceeded).

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web using a self-hosted SearXNG instance. Returns titles, URLs, and snippets.

tools.name: write

# EDITORIAL_FEEDBACK.md — News Card Editorial Feedback

Handles Telegram feedback on published news cards. **Not part of the crypto pipeline.**

---

## When this applies

| Pattern | Example |
|---------|---------|
| Callback `oc_r:` / `oc_ri:` / `oc_ri_menu:` | Rate article or image |
| Callback `oc_draft:` / `oc_draft_yes:` / `oc_draft_no:` | Unpublish flow |
| Callback `oc_publish:` / `oc_publish_yes:` / `oc_publish_no:` | Publish flow |
| Callback `oc_edit:` / `oc_edit_apply:` / `oc_edit_cancel:` | Edit flow |
| Text | `RATE 8`, `IMAGE 7`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` |
| Document reply | `.md` file replying to bot's edit prompt |

---

## What to do

1. **Do NOT** start or continue the crypto news pipeline.
2. **Do NOT** spawn subagents.
3. Run the handler immediately:

```bash
python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace-orchestrator/skills/pipeline/handle_card_feedback.py \
  --payload "<callback data if present>" \
  --message-text "<user text if present>" \
  --chat-id "<telegram chat id>" \
  --user-id "<telegram user id>" \
  --username "<telegram username if known>" \
  --reply-to-message-id "<replied-to message id if present>" \
  --document-file-id "<telegram file_id if document upload>" \
  --document-name "<original filename if document upload>"
```

4. **If the handler already sent a Telegram reply, do NOT repeat stdout in the group — end turn silently.**
5. If handler failed before replying, show the stdout line to the user.

---

## Pipeline vs feedback

| User says | Route |
|-----------|-------|
| `run pipeline`, `run crypto news pipeline` | SOUL.md pipeline |
| RATE, IMAGE, DRAFT, PUBLISH, EDIT, callback taps, edit `.md` upload | This doc |

Pipeline takes precedence only when the message explicitly requests the pipeline.

---

## PUBLISH flow notes

- Tap **Publish** or reply `PUBLISH` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, publish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `publish` (live on site).
- If already published → bot replies "already published".

---

## EDIT flow notes

- Tap **Edit** or reply `EDIT` to the news card.
- Bot sends `article-{run_id}.md` as a document.
- Download → edit → **save** → reply to that document with a corrected **`.md` file** (not pasted text).
- Identical upload (no changes) → bot replies "No changes detected" and keeps the edit session open (`EDIT_UNCHANGED`).
- Changed upload → bot shows **+N / −M lines** summary plus **Apply to WordPress** / **Cancel** buttons.
- After apply on a draft → bot offers a **Publish** button on the confirmation message.
- Pasted text during edit → handler returns `EDIT_USE_DOCUMENT`.

### Document reply — CRITICAL routing rule

When the user replies to the bot's edit prompt with a `.md` document:

1. **Always** call the handler with `--document-file-id` from the **user's uploaded document** in the current message metadata.
2. **Never** read `media/inbound/tmp*.md` from reply context — that is often the **bot's original unedited file** bundled with the user's upload.
3. **Never** call `handle_edit_document()` manually with a local path. The handler downloads the file from Telegram via `file_id`.
4. Set `--reply-to-message-id` to the **bot edit prompt message id** (the document the user replied to).

Wrong file selection causes false `EDIT_UNCHANGED` even when the user's saved file has real edits.

---

## DRAFT flow notes

- Tap **Unpublish** or reply `DRAFT` to the card.
- Confirm with **Yes, unpublish** / **Cancel**.
- Sets WordPress post status to `draft`.

---

## Mention rules

- Callback taps: no `@mention` needed.
- Reply to news card: `RATE`, `DRAFT`, `PUBLISH`, `EDIT` work without `@mention`.
- Reply to bot edit prompt with `.md`: works via `reply_to_bot` implicit mention.

# Ondo Finance Founder Nathan Allman Dies Unexpectedly at 32

The decentralized finance community is mourning the sudden passing of Nathan Allman, the founder and CEO of real-world asset (RWA) platform Ondo Finance. The company confirmed on [May 26, 2026](https://x.com/OndoFinance/status/2059054473775894797?ref=blockhead.co), that Allman, a key figure in the tokenization movement, died unexpectedly at 32. His work was instrumental in bridging traditional financial assets with blockchain technology.

Under Allman’s leadership, Ondo Finance became a dominant force in the RWA sector, bringing over $3.86 billion in tokenized assets on-chain. The news shocked the industry, where Allman was respected as a brilliant pioneer. [In an official statement](https://cointelegraph.com/news/ondo-finance-founder-nathan-allman-passes-away-aged-32), the company honored his legacy and his mission to create a more open financial system.

Allman’s belief in technology's power to democratize finance was the cornerstone of Ondo’s philosophy. The platform he created serves over 111,680 token holders, offering them on-chain access to U.S. Treasuries, stocks, and other assets. [His untimely death](https://blockhead.co/2026/05/26/ondo-finance-ceo-nathan-allman-dies-unexpectedly) leaves a void, but his work established a critical foundation for asset tokenization.

## Allman's Legacy in RWA Tokenization

Nathan Allman was a key architect of the tokenized RWA movement. His work with Ondo Finance helped to legitimize and popularize the concept of bringing traditional financial assets onto the blockchain. This process, known as tokenization, creates a digital representation of an asset, allowing it to be traded with the efficiency and transparency of cryptocurrency. Allman’s contributions were critical in demonstrating the viability of this model at an institutional scale.

### A Pioneer in On-Chain Assets

The $3.86 billion in assets tokenized under Allman's watch is a clear metric of his success. The range of assets, from U.S. Treasuries to equities, showcased the breadth of his ambition. He understood that for blockchain to achieve mainstream adoption, it needed to integrate with the existing financial system. This pragmatic approach allowed Ondo to build trust and attract capital from both crypto-native investors and traditional finance entities. Allman's work provided a clear roadmap for how to structure and manage tokenized RWAs, setting an industry standard.

### From Traditional Finance to Web3

Allman's unique background gave him the ideal skill set to pioneer the RWA space. He founded Ondo Finance in 2021 after working on Goldman Sachs' digital assets desk, which gave him firsthand knowledge of the institutional world’s needs. Before his time at Goldman, he founded ChainStreet Capital, a crypto hedge fund focused on algorithmic trading. An alumnus of Brown University and Stanford, his combined experience in Wall Street and crypto was a key ingredient in Ondo’s ability to navigate the complex regulatory and technical challenges of tokenization.

One of Allman’s most significant achievements was capturing the attention of giants like BlackRock. The world’s largest asset manager has identified tokenization as a transformative technology. Allman’s work at Ondo provided a tangible proof of concept, demonstrating that tokenization could be done securely and at scale. This helped de-risk the concept for larger institutions, and his ability to articulate this vision was instrumental in driving the dialogue around institutional adoption.

## Leadership Continuity and Market Reaction

In the wake of the tragic news, Ondo Finance acted swiftly to ensure stability. The company announced that its president, Ian De Bode, would immediately step into the role of CEO. This move indicates a robust succession plan was in place, a testament to Allman's foresight in building a resilient organization. De Bode is a seasoned leader with a deep background in digital assets and strategy, making him a natural choice to guide the company.

### Ian De Bode Appointed CEO

Ian De Bode's journey to the CEO position was a deliberate one. He joined Ondo as Chief Strategy Officer in late 2023 and was promoted to president in November 2025. This progression shows the level of trust Allman had placed in him. His promotion to CEO is the final step in a leadership track that was already well underway, ensuring the company's long-term health.

De Bode expressed his sadness at the loss of his friend and mentor while reaffirming his commitment to their shared mission. He told Cointelegraph, "The mission of Ondo, Nate's mission, has not changed. If Nate were here, he would want to continue executing with excellence. We will make him proud." This sentiment was echoed by other leaders at the company, providing a strong foundation as they navigate this difficult period.

### ONDO Token Remains Stable

The news had a relatively muted impact on the price of ONDO, the platform’s governance token. In the 24 hours following the announcement, ONDO traded at approximately $0.43, a modest decline of around 3%. The token's stability in the face of such a significant event can be seen as a sign of underlying market confidence in the company's future.

The limited price impact suggests investors believe in the resilience of the organization Allman built. The swift appointment of Ian De Bode as CEO, along with clear communication from the leadership team, likely played a crucial role in preventing a more severe reaction. This market response underscores the confidence that the community has in the new CEO and the existing team to carry Allman's legacy forward.

## Conclusion

The sudden death of Nathan Allman is a profound loss for the crypto industry. As a pioneer, his work with Ondo Finance laid a critical foundation for tokenizing real-world assets. The passing of Ondo Finance Nathan Allman leaves a significant void, but his legacy is cemented in the resilient company he built. With a strong succession plan and a clear mission, the market has shown its belief that Ondo Finance will continue to lead the charge in bridging traditional finance and the blockchain. The company's commitment to executing Allman’s vision will be the ultimate tribute to his work.

The new CEO of Ondo Finance is Ian De Bode. He previously served as the company's president and chief strategy officer. His appointment was part of a planned succession, ensuring leadership continuity.

The ONDO governance token saw a mild decline of about 3%, trading near $0.43 in the 24 hours after the news. This relative stability is seen by many as a sign of the market's confidence in the company's resilience and its new leadership.
